target_claim: The identity reduction G' = G satisfies the biconditional: G is 3-colorable if and only if G' is 12-colorable. The reverse direction is false, so the reduction does not establish NP-hardness as claimed.
source_quote:
Let G′ be the same graph as G, i.e., G′ = (V, E).
... We need to show that G is 3-colorable if and only if G′ is 12-colorable.
test_sketch: Implement the reduction exactly as written: reduce(G) returns G unchanged (a few lines of Python). Claimed property: G is 3-colorable iff reduce(G) is 12-colorable. Oracle: brute-force k-colorability by trying all k^n assignments for n <= 12 vertices. Input family: small non-3-colorable graphs, e.g., G = K4 (4 vertices, 6 edges). Brute force shows K4 is NOT 3-colorable but reduce(K4) = K4 IS 12-colorable (any 4 of the 12 colors work), directly refuting the claimed biconditional on a 4-vertex input. Also fails on K5..K12, and on the Groetzsch graph (11 vertices, chromatic number 4). The solution's own (<=) argument on lines 0017-0022 is also refuted: a 12-coloring f' of K4 using colors c11, c12, c13, c21 maps under their index rule to f-values 1,2,3,1 on two adjacent vertices, which is not a proper 3-coloring.
